note: All figures are FACT, transcribed verbatim from GSK results releases in sources.json. Interpretations are labeled ai_hypothesis and are separated from fact.

fact.segment_commentary: Growth driven mainly by Specialty Medicines, with double-digit sales growth in Respiratory, Immunology & Inflammation, Oncology and HIV (Luke Miels).

quarters.ai_hypothesis: A £32.7bn base growing at +7% CER with a Specialty-led mix implies a durable, reinvestment-capable P&L that can sustain multi-year outsourced commercialization spend.

segments.name: General Medicines
segments.note: Decline driven by genericization of the older established portfolio.

fact.franchise_highlights: Shingrix delivered more than £1.0bn (+20%), a record quarter; HIV sales £1.8bn (+10%).

quarters.ai_hypothesis: Specialty +14% versus General Medicines -6% confirms an accelerating budget shift toward growth franchises, concentrating services demand in Specialty and Vaccines.

segments.name: Specialty Medicines
segments.note: Led by continued launch of Nucala in COPD and HIV medicines Cabenuva and Dovato.

segments.name: Vaccines
segments.note: Helped by international expansion of Arexvy, meningitis vaccines and Shingrix in Europe.

segments.name: General Medicines
segments.note: Declining sales of the older established portfolio amid competition and genericization.

quarters.ai_hypothesis: Specialty and Vaccines now materially outweigh a shrinking General Medicines segment; the launch-driven Specialty engine is the highest-priority target for commercialization services.

fact.long_term_2031_outlook: More than £40bn sales; accelerating growth from 2031 onwards

guidance.ai_hypothesis: Narrowing 2026 guidance to the upper half plus a reaffirmed >£40bn 2031 target signals management confidence and a stable-to-expanding services budget environment favorable to multi-year engagements.
